I: terminal incumbent mass of the tracked component, read from the per-block snapshot at terminal_time

I0.definition: the block's own incumbent mass recorded at t256
I0.implementation: dr05_flux_decomposition.py line 78: I0 = num(r['I0']) read PER ROW, i.e. per (size, block, arm)
I0.is_it_condition_specific: recorded per arm, but audited identical across arms within a block
I0.recomputed_for_each_eligible_set_size: NOT_APPLICABLE - no size ladder was ever run with this estimator

I_over_T: line 107: I_over_T_treated = It / Tt, where T is the terminal total tracked mass
frozen_denominator_rule_for_any_successo: I0 must be the block's own t256 incumbent mass, never recomputed per condition and never pooled across blocks

does_a_prior_size_normalized_estimand_ex.consequence: section 4 forbids inventing one merely because the mission is named 'size-normalized'. No secondary normalization is defined here.

eligible_set_cardinality_distribution.what_exists: a single recorded scalar, median_eligible_sink_sites_per_event = 1, in dr05_mechanism_adjudication.json
eligible_set_cardinality_distribution.where_it_could_come_from: P07's surviving per-event ledgers P07/p07a_event_ledger.csv.gz and P07/p07b_event_ledger.csv.gz - recomputable with ZERO engine runs

independent_unit: one seed block = one world per condition; the protocol forbids treating the 144 logical trajectories as 144 independent units
primary_endpoint_is_a_median: yes - every I_over_I0 figure in the prior evidence is a median over blocks, so a successor must use the pre-existing definition and a paired world-level interval, not a mean
